solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Nameless clarinetist perhaps performing in concert (10)

indicatorNotes.Nameless: Something nameless has lost its name, and N is the standard abbreviation for name, so the fodder drops its N.
indicatorNotes.performing: Performers put on an act, so the letters are made to act out a new order.

blocks.note: the eleven letters of the musician with N (name) taken out

annotation.surface: An unnamed clarinet player giving a concert.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the fodder: a clarinetist playing a concert is one example of the answer, hence 'perhaps'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a solo player giving a recital, such as a clarinetist on stage, is a recitalist.

entries.clue: Capital of two US states (4)

blocks.note: the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

annotation.surface: A trivia question about a city serving as seat of government for two American states.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface asks for an American capital; the answer is a European one built from two postal abbreviations.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Latvian seat of government is one of Europe's capital cities.

entries.clue: Happen to turn round (4,5)

blocks.note: the sailing sense: swing onto the other tack

annotation.surface: Someone who chances to turn and look behind them.
annotation.walkthrough: The second sense is nautical: a sailing boat comes about when it swings onto the other tack.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one phrasal verb: everyday 'occur', and the sailor's word for going about onto a new tack.

entries.clue: Play awful when trite and no longer fresh (3,7,4)

indicatorNotes.awful: Something awful is in a terrible state, so the letters of 'when trite' are to be put in a different one.

annotation.surface: A drama critic panning a play as hackneyed and stale.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a bad review, which conceals that 'Play' is the definition and names one of Shakespeare's.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is one of Shakespeare's late plays.

entries.clue: Weapon for which one keeps one’s head down a good while? (7)

annotation.definition: Weapon for which one keeps one’s head down a good while?

blocks.note: the surface reading: a weapon you use while ducking, as in a trench

blocks.clueFragment: keeps one’s head down a good while
blocks.note: the setter's reading: a head lowered for a lengthy time makes an extended bow

annotation.surface: A soldier keeping their head low for safety while using some weapon.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the weapon's name as two words: a LONG BOW is what you make if you keep your head down a good while.
annotation.definitionFit: The weapon is the tall medieval English bow; the question mark flags the pun on bowing one's head.

entries.clue: More than one cut, not quite every one (7)

indicatorNotes.not quite: Something not quite complete falls just short, so the word for 'every one' loses its last letter.

blocks.note: ALL (every one) minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A remark that more than one got cut, though not all of them.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a single statement about cuts; 'More than one' is the definition and the rest builds it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: several means a number greater than one but not many.

entries.clue: Nitrogen in cigarette that delivers poison (4)

annotation.definitionNote: a relative clause standing for the noun: the thing that delivers poison

indicatorNotes.in: Nitrogen is literally placed in the cigarette, so its symbol sits inside the slang word.

blocks.note: the chemical symbol, placed after FA

annotation.surface: A health warning about the toxic compounds in cigarette smoke.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes the cigarette the poisoner; the definition is the snake's tooth. A fag is British slang for a cigarette.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a snake's hollow tooth is what injects its venom.

entries.clue: Past river, a market (5)

blocks.note: in the past, as in 'long ago'

annotation.surface: Directions: go past the river and you reach a market.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Past' as a preposition of place; it is the adverb of time.
annotation.definitionFit: A historical sense: the open square of an ancient Greek city served as its marketplace.

entries.clue: With vegetables, pull up grass (10)

indicatorNotes.up: In a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the word for 'pull' is written backwards.

blocks.note: as a horse draws a cart

annotation.surface: A gardener lifting vegetables and weeding the grass.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pull up' looks like a gardening phrase, but 'pull' is DRAW and 'up' turns it round in this down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary word: an expanse of grassy turf is what old writers called by this name.

entries.clue: Leaving an unfinished task and settling down (8,6)

indicatorNotes.unfinished: An unfinished job lacks its ending, so the word for task loses its last letter.

blocks.note: abandoning, as in dropping a subject

annotation.surface: Someone abandoning a half-done job to put their feet up.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one lazy action; 'Leaving an unfinished task' is all wordplay and 'settling down' alone defines.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative use of a nautical phrase: a ship that stops and stays put has settled, as a person does.

entries.clue: I want a little something immediately (5)

indicatorNotes.a little: A little of something is a small part of it, so the answer is a small part of the next two words.

blocks.note: the last letter of the first word and the first four of the second

annotation.surface: An impatient child demanding a treat right now.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is a slurred 'give me', the very cry the surface is acting out.
annotation.definitionFit: A colloquial idiom: the slurred demand for something is how a grabby child says it wants it.

entries.clue: Always behind rear of column: not again! (9)

indicatorNotes.behind: Behind means following on, so the word for always is placed after the letter.
indicatorNotes.rear of: The rear of a column is its tail end, so take the last letter of the word.

annotation.surface: A soldier stuck forever at the back of a marching column, vowing never again.
annotation.walkthrough: The word is the refrain of Poe's poem 'The Raven'.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary synonym: the exclamation means never again.

entries.clue: Plausibly, rains ruined army training here (9,5)

indicatorNotes.ruined: Something ruined is wrecked and must be rebuilt, so the letters are reassembled.

annotation.surface: An excuse that bad weather spoilt an army exercise.
annotation.walkthrough: This is a large chalk plateau in Wiltshire, England, used by the British Army as its main training ground.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the British Army has trained on this Wiltshire plateau for over a century.

entries.clue: Go canoeing for relaxation, but not in such a craft (5-5)

annotation.definitionNote: the answer describes the craft: a canoe is not an ocean-going vessel

indicatorNotes.for relaxation: Relaxation is a loosening, and letters loosened up are free to settle in a new order.

annotation.surface: Advice to paddle a canoe for leisure, but to keep off the open sea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For relaxation' reads as the reason to paddle; it is the anagram signal. The definition works by contrast: a canoe is no ship for the open sea.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by contrast: a canoe is the opposite of a vessel built for the open sea.

entries.clue: Native American chief’s first love arrested by guard taken back (7)

indicatorNotes.first: The first of a word is its opening letter, so chief gives C.
indicatorNotes.arrested by: Someone arrested is held by the police, so love is held inside the word for guard.
indicatorNotes.taken back: Taking something back returns it the way it came, so the guard with love inside is written backwards.

blocks.note: love = nil = O in tennis, placed between WATC and H

annotation.surface: A tribal chief's sweetheart seized by a sentry.
annotation.walkthrough: The chief's first letter stands outside the reversal; only WATCH with O inside it is turned round.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is one of the Native American peoples of the south-eastern United States.

entries.clue: Look after youngster grabbing one whiskey that’s downed (4,3)

indicatorNotes.after: After means coming later in order, so the word for look is placed after the boy.
indicatorNotes.grabbing: Grabbing is taking hold of, so the youngster closes around the one.

blocks.note: W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Minding a young person who has drunk a whiskey and passed out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Look after' reads as 'take care of'; it is LO placed after the next piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: knocked down or brought low, as by illness or a blow.

entries.clue: Stories about endlessly pompous rituals (9)

indicatorNotes.about: About means around, so the word for stories goes around the other piece.
indicatorNotes.endlessly: Without its end, the word for pompous loses its last letter.

blocks.note: fibs, as when a child tells stories

annotation.surface: Tall tales told around solemn ceremonies.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stories' here are fibs, as in a child telling stories.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: set forms of public worship are religious rituals.

entries.clue: Insects eating live one of the Scorpion group (7)

indicatorNotes.eating: Whatever is eaten ends up inside the eater, so the insects take the other piece in.

annotation.surface: Insects devouring a live scorpion.
annotation.walkthrough: The Scorpion group is the constellation Scorpius, not a family of creatures.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this red giant is the brightest star in the constellation of the Scorpion.

entries.clue: Postponed decision about small particle (5,2)

blocks.note: a subatomic particle such as the electron

annotation.surface: A physicist putting off a verdict on a tiny particle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' belongs to the definition: the phrase means putting off a decision about something overnight.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: if you sleep on a problem you delay deciding until the next day.

entries.clue: Aircraft following large boat, heading off (7)

indicatorNotes.heading off: A heading is what comes at the top, so taking it off removes the boat's first letter.

blocks.note: f. = following, as in page references
LIGHTER, a big flat-bottomed barge, without its first letter

annotation.surface: A plane tailing a big ship, then turning away.
annotation.walkthrough: A lighter is a barge used to ferry cargo to and from ships; FREIGHTER tempts, but it would need three letters off.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a fast military plane built for air combat is one kind of aircraft.

entries.clue: Wrong order at first of rising problem in flock (4,3)

indicatorNotes.at first: What comes at first is at the very start, so order gives only its opening letter.
indicatorNotes.rising: In a down entry, rising means reading upwards, so the assembled pieces are written backwards.

annotation.surface: A shepherd noticing that something is out of order in the flock.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wrong order' looks like one phrase, but 'Wrong' is TORT alone and 'order' only lends its O.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: this hoof infection of sheep is a common trouble for a flock.

entries.clue: Leave London, hoping to be returned? (2,2,3,7)

blocks.note: head out of the city for rural parts
a British government calling a general election, hoping voters return it to office

annotation.surface: A Londoner off to the countryside, hoping to come back.
annotation.walkthrough: In British politics a prime minister calls a general election by this phrase, hoping to be returned to office.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a literal trip out of town, and the British idiom for putting a government before the voters.

entries.clue: Delicious pie with a different crust (5)

indicatorNotes.with a different crust: A crust is the outside of a pie, so the pie's outer letter at the front is changed.

blocks.note: a folded pastry pie, like the Cornish pasty

annotation.surface: A pie that tastes great because of a new pastry.
annotation.walkthrough: A pasty is a folded pastry pie with a savoury filling, a British staple.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: food that is pleasing to eat is both.

entries.clue: Not straight, because bent (4)

annotation.surface: Something called crooked because it is bent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bent' is a noun here, an inclination. 'Not straight' reads as a second definition but builds the first two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the noun: a bent is a natural leaning, as a bias is.

entries.clue: Abuse involving American pair leading orchestra and conductor? Absolutely not (9)

indicatorNotes.involving: To involve is to take something in, so the word for abuse wraps round the American.
indicatorNotes.leading: What leads is at the front, so the pair is the first two letters of orchestra.

blocks.note: the first two letters of orchestra

annotation.surface: A scandal about an American duo mistreating an orchestra and its conductor.
annotation.walkthrough: The orchestra and conductor are musical in the surface; the definition means an electrical conductor, of which the answer is the opposite.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by contrast: a material that blocks electric current is the opposite of a conductor.

entries.clue: Hot island? One part of island (5)

blocks.note: an ait is a small river island, as in the Thames

annotation.surface: A question whether an island is hot, answered with a geography lesson.
annotation.walkthrough: An ait (or eyot) is a British word for an islet in a river. The country shares Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic, which makes the definition fair.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: this country occupies the western third of the island of Hispaniola.

entries.clue: Artist’s spiritual exercises transferring pieces in odd places (4)

indicatorNotes.transferring pieces in odd places: Pieces moved between the odd-numbered places swap round, so the first and third letters trade.

blocks.note: the Indian discipline of meditation and posture; Y and G, in places one and three, swap

annotation.surface: A painter's meditative routine with the props moved about.
annotation.walkthrough: Only the odd-numbered letters move: Y and G swap, O and A stay put.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Francisco Goya was a Spanish painter.

entries.clue: One has confidence in investments (4,6)

annotation.surface: An investor who believes in the stock market.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like part of 'confidence in', but it joins wordplay to definition. A unit trust is the British name for a mutual fund.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: pooled funds are one kind of investment, the British counterpart of mutual funds.
